In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Fatir

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers having wings, two, three, or four﴾, to the end of the verse.

The alif and lam in His saying "al-hamdu lillah" ("All praise is due to Allah") are for comprehensiveness (istighraq), meaning that all praise belongs to Allah, glorified and exalted is He. Allah, exalted is He, has praised Himself with this great praise, teaching His creation in His Book to praise Him with it. This is joined with His being ﴿Creator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers﴾. This indicates that His creating the heavens and the earth, and what is mentioned with it, points to His greatness, the perfection of His power, and His deserving of praise for His own essence, because of His majesty and the perfection of His power. Besides this, in the creation of the heavens and the earth there are blessings upon the children of Adam. So He deserves praise for His essence through their creation, and for His bestowing favour upon creation by them. The fact that their creation combines the deserving of both of the praises mentioned is shown by verses from the Book of Allah.

As for the fact that this requires praising Allah for His greatness and perfection, and His deserving every beautiful praise, it has come in verses from the Book of Allah, the Exalted:

• Like His saying, exalted is He, at the beginning of the surah "al-An'am" (The Cattle): ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light﴾ to the end of the verse [Al-An'am: 1],

• And His saying at the beginning of the surah "Saba'" (Sheba): ﴿All praise is due to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ to the end of the verse [Saba': 2],

• And His saying, exalted is He, at the beginning of the surah "al-Fatihah" (The Opening): ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-Fatihah: 2]. We have already mentioned that His saying "Lord of the worlds" is explained by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Pharaoh said, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?" [Moses] said, "Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you should be certain."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 23-24],

• Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And peace upon the messengers. And praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [As-Saffat: 181-182],

• And His saying: ﴿And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75].

As for His deserving praise for His creation by creating the heavens and the earth, because of the blessing He bestowed upon the children of Adam in that, it has come in verses from the Book of Allah. Exalted is He has made clear that He bestowed favour upon His creation by subjecting to them (sakhkhara lahum) what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, in verses from His Book:

• Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 13],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, constant [in their courses]﴾ to the end of the verse [Ibrahim: 33],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the sun and the moon and the stars are subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-A'raf: 54].

We have already mentioned the verses that clarify the meaning of the subjection of what is in the heavens to the people of the earth, in the surah "al-Hijr" (The Rocky Tract), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We guarded it from every accursed devil﴾ to the end of the verse [Al-Hijr: 17].

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿who made the angels messengers﴾. We have already mentioned the verses that clarify it in the surah "al-Hajj" (The Pilgrimage), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from the angels and from mankind﴾ [Al-Hajj: 75].

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿Creator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and their originator without any previous pattern.

Ibn Kathir, may God have mercy on him, said in his tafsir of this noble verse: Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "I did not know what 'Fatir of the heavens and the earth' meant until two Bedouins came to me disputing over a well, and one of them said to his companion, 'I am the one who fatartuha (initiated/began it),' meaning: I began it."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whatever mercy Allah opens to the people, none can withhold it, and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him﴾, and so on. In this noble verse He, may He be exalted and sublime, has mentioned that whatever mercy and favour He opens to the people, with all kinds of blessings, no one, whoever he may be, is able to withhold it from them; and whatever He withholds from them of His mercy and favour, no one, whoever he may be, is able to send it to them. This is known necessarily from the religion (ma'lum bi-l-darurah min al-din). The mercy mentioned in the verse is general in everything by which Allah shows mercy to His creation of blessings, worldly and otherwise, such as His opening for them the mercy of rain; as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So look at the traces of Allah's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death﴾ [al-Rum: 50].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He it is who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾ [al-A'raf: 57], and His saying: ﴿And He it is who sends down the rain after they had despaired, and spreads His mercy﴾ [al-Shura: 28]. And among His mercy is the sending of messengers and the sending down of books, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, except as a mercy from your Lord﴾ [al-Qasas: 86], as its explanation has already preceded in surah "al-Kahf", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they found a servant of Our servants, whom We had given mercy from Us﴾ [al-Kahf: 65], and so on.

What this noble verse includes has been clarified in many verses:

• such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it but He; and if He intends for you good, none can repel His bounty﴾ [Yunus: 107],

• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm, or intends for you mercy?﴾ [al-Fath: 11],

• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you evil, or intends for you mercy?﴾ [al-Ahzab: 17],

and other verses besides these.

We have already presented some discussion of this in surah "al-An'am", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it but He; and if He touches you with good, then He is Able over all things﴾ [al-An'am: 17]. As for "mā" in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whatever Allah opens﴾ [Fatir: 2], and His saying: ﴿and whatever He withholds﴾, they are conditional (shartiyyah). The opening of a thing is enabling access to it and removing the barriers before it, while withholding is contrary to that.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven?﴾ The interrogation in His saying ﴿Is there any creator other than Allah﴾ is one of denial (inkari), so it implies the meaning of negation.

The meaning is: there is no creator except Allah alone, and the Creator is the one who alone deserves worship (ibadah).

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in surah "al-Ra'd," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or have they assigned to Allah partners who created like His creation?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 16]. And in surah "al-Furqan," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they have taken, besides Him, gods who create nothing while they themselves are created﴾ [al-Furqan: 3], and in other places besides these.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿who provides for you from the heaven and the earth﴾ indicates that He alone is the Provider, and that creation is in utmost need of Him, may He be exalted.

The verses indicating this are many, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Who is it that can provide for you if He withholds His provision?﴾ [al-Mulk: 21], (p-279) and His saying: ﴿So seek provision from Allah﴾ [al-Ankabut: 17].

We have already presented many of the verses indicating this in surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [al-Isra': 9].

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then messengers before you were denied. And to Allah are returned [all] matters.﴾ What this noble verse contains is consolation for him (ﷺ): that what he encountered from his people of denial, the noble messengers before him encountered from their own peoples, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all. This is made clear in many verses, such as the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And already were messengers denied before you, but they were patient over that with which they were denied and harmed until Our victory came to them﴾ [al-An'am: 34], and the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you﴾ [Fussilat: 43]. The verses of similar meaning are many and well known.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾.

We have already presented the verses that have this meaning in several places of this blessed Book, such as His saying, exalted is He, in "al-Kahf" (the Cave): ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me, while they are an enemy to you?﴾ [al-Kahf: 50], and the verse continues.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in surah "al-Hajj" (the Pilgrimage), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It has been decreed for him that whoever takes him as an ally, he will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [al-Hajj: 4].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So let not your soul waste away in regret over them﴾. We have already presented the verses clarifying this in Surat al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you﴾ [al-An'am: 33]. And in al-Kahf, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their footsteps﴾ and so on [al-Kahf: 6], and in other places.

Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and revive thereby the earth after its death. Thus will be the resurrection.﴾ What this noble verse contains, namely that His reviving of the earth after its death, which is witnessed in the life of this world, is a decisive proof of His power over the resurrection (al-ba'th), has already been explained with Qur'anic verses in many places (p-280) in Surat al-Baqarah, al-Nahl, al-Anbiya' and elsewhere, and reference to it has been made repeatedly before.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 10:

Allah's saying: ﴿Whoever desires honour—to Allah belongs all honour.﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, makes clear that whoever desires honour, all of it belongs to Allah alone. So let him seek it from Him, and let him take the means to attain it by obeying Him, Majestic and Exalted, for whoever obeys Him, He grants him honour in this world and the Hereafter. As for those who worship idols in order to attain honour through their worship, and those who take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, seeking honour from them, they are in error and blindness regarding the truth, because they seek honour from a place of humiliation.

This meaning indicated by this noble verse is clarified in verses of the Book of Allah, Exalted:

• such as His saying: ﴿And they have taken gods besides Allah that they might be for them a source of honour. No! They will reject their worship of them and will be against them opponents﴾ [Maryam: 81–82],

• and His saying: ﴿Those who take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them? Indeed, all honour belongs to Allah﴾ [an-Nisa': 139],

• and His saying: ﴿And let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, all honour belongs to Allah; He is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾ [Yunus: 65],

• and His saying: ﴿They say, "If we return to Madinah, the more honourable will surely expel therefrom the more humble." And to Allah belongs honour, and to His Messenger and to the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8], and His saying: ﴿Exalted is your Lord, the Lord of honour, above what they describe﴾ [as-Saffat: 180].

Al-'Izzah (honour) means dominance and strength. From it is the saying of al-Khansa':

"As if they had never been a protected sanctuary, when people, at that time, were those who were powerful (ʿazīz)."

That is: whoever dominates, plunders. From it is His saying: ﴿and he overpowered me in the argument﴾ [Sad: 23], meaning: he overcame me and prevailed over me in the dispute.

As for the statement of some scholars that the meaning of the verse, ﴿whoever desires honour﴾, is: whoever wishes to know to whom honour truly belongs, the point we have mentioned is more correct. And Allah knows best.

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿And those who plot evil deeds—for them is a severe punishment﴾, the verse. Some discussion of it has already preceded in Surah an-Nahl, along with the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of as-sayyi'at (the evil deeds).

We have previously mentioned in other places that among their plotting of evil deeds is their disbelief in Allah and their commanding their followers to it, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, it was the plotting of night and day when you were ordering us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him."﴾ [Saba': 33], and as His saying, Exalted: ﴿And they planned a great plot and said, "Do not leave your gods; do not leave Wadd or Suwa' or Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr."﴾ [Nuh: 22–23]. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah created you from dust, then from a drop of semen﴾. Its clarification has already been given with the Qur'anic verses at the beginning of surah "al-Hajj", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, indeed We created you from dust﴾ [al-Hajj: 5], and so on.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in surah "ar-Ra'd", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah knows what every female carries, and what the wombs fall short of and what they increase. And everything with Him is in measure﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 8], together with an explanation of the rulings related to the verse.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And no one is granted a lifespan nor is anything lessened of his lifespan except that it is in a Book﴾. We have already presented some discussion of it at the end of surah "al-Ahzab", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And mankind carried it; indeed he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72]. And in surah "al-Furqan", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He placed therein a lamp and a moon giving light﴾ [al-Furqan: 61].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-375) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surah Fatir

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And no one is granted a lifespan nor is anything lessened of his lifespan except that it is in a Book﴾.

The pronoun in His saying "'umurihi" (his lifespan) apparently refers back to "mu'ammar" (one granted a lifespan), so the meaning of the verse becomes problematic, because "mu'ammar" and "man 'umurihi yunqas" (one whose lifespan is lessened) are opposites, so the contradiction between the pronoun and its referent appears.

The answer is that what is meant by "mu'ammar" here is the category of "mu'ammar", which is any person in general. It therefore applies both to the one whose lifespan is not lessened and to the one whose lifespan is lessened. So the meaning becomes: no one's lifespan is increased, nor is anyone's lifespan lessened, except that it is in a Book.

This issue is the one known among the scholars of Arabic grammar as the issue of: "'indi dirham wa nisfuhu" (I have a dirham and its half), i.e., half of another dirham.

Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir: The pronoun refers to the category, not to the individual, because the one who is long-lived is in the Book and in Allah's knowledge, and his lifespan is not lessened. The pronoun refers to the category, end quote.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And the two seas are not alike: this one is sweet, palatable, pleasant to drink, and that one is salty, bitter﴾. Its explanation has already been given in surah "al-Furqan," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who released the two seas, this one sweet, palatable, and that one salty, bitter﴾ [al-Furqan: 53].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And from each you eat fresh flesh and extract ornaments that you wear﴾. The discussion of it has already been given, along with an elaboration of the legal rulings (fiqh) related to this, in surah "al-Nahl," in (p-282) the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who subjected the sea that you might eat from it fresh flesh and extract from it ornaments that you wear﴾ [al-Nahl: 14].

And it has already been given in surah "al-An'am," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-An'am: 130]. That His saying in this verse of "Fatir": ﴿And from each you eat fresh flesh and extract ornaments that you wear﴾ is a clear Qur'anic evidence against the claim of those scholars who asserted that pearls and coral come forth only from the salt sea exclusively.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 14:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will disavow your association of them﴾ — the verse. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Maryam," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No! They will deny their worship of them and will be opponents to them﴾ [Maryam: 82], and in other places.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾. In this noble verse, exalted and high is He, He made clear that He is free of need from His creation, and that His creation is in need of Him. That is, He commands them and forbids them not in order to benefit from their obedience, nor to repel harm by their disobedience. Rather, the benefit in all of that is for them. He, exalted and high is He, is the Free of need by His very essence, with absolute independence.

What this noble verse indicates, although it is known as a matter of religion by necessity, has come in many places in the Book of Allah.

• Such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is the Free of need, and you are the poor. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people﴾ [Muhammad: 38],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was free of need. And Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy﴾ [At-Taghabun: 6],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Musa said, "If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth entirely, then indeed, Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy"﴾ [Ibrahim: 8],

along with other verses besides these.

And by this you know the enormity of the slander of ﴿those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 181]. Allah has threatened them for that, by His saying: ﴿We will record what they have said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 181].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If He wills, He will remove you and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for Allah.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "An-Nisa'" (Women), in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If He wills, He will remove you, O mankind, and bring others; and ever is Allah capable of that.﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:133]

(p-283) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify it, together with the answer to some of the questions directed at the verse in the surah "Banī Isrā'īl," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isrā' 17:15].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if one heavily laden calls [another] to [carry] its load, nothing of it will be carried, even by a near relative﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify it in the surah "al-Naḥl," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection and [also] bear burdens from those whom they misled without knowledge. Unfortunate is what they bear﴾ [al-Naḥl 16:25]. The way to reconcile verses like this one with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [al-'Ankabūt 29:13], and similar verses, is [explained there].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord in the unseen and establish prayer﴾. In this noble verse, may He be exalted and high, He mentioned that his warning (ﷺ) is restricted to those who fear their Lord in the unseen and establish prayer. This restriction is relative, because they are the ones who benefit from the warning, and one who does not benefit from the warning is as if he and one who was never warned are equal, since both gain nothing.

This meaning is made clear in verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe. You can only warn one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful in the unseen﴾ [Yā-Sīn 36:10–11], and His saying: ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾ [al-Nāzi'āt 79:45]. Generally similar in meaning is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My warning﴾ [Qāf 50:45]. We have already presented the meaning of warning (indhār, giving warning) and its types, clarified in the surah "al-A'rāf," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So let there be no discomfort in your breast from it, that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers﴾ [al-A'rāf 7:2].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the blind and the seeing are not alike﴾. We have already explained this with the verses at the beginning of Surah Hud, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The likeness of the two parties is as the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing﴾ [Hud: 24] and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the living and the dead are not alike﴾. Al-ahya' (the living) here means the believers, and al-amwat (the dead) means the disbelievers. So life here is the life of faith, and death is the death of disbelief.

This meaning is made clear in other places, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is he who was dead and We brought him to life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness, never to emerge from it?﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. His saying, "Is he who was dead," means dead in disbelief, and "We brought him to life" means brought to the life of faith. Likewise His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That He may warn whoever is alive and that the word may be justified against the disbelievers﴾ [Ya-Sin: 70]. It is understood from His saying, ﴿whoever is alive﴾, that is, one with the life of faith, that the disbelievers against whom the word is justified are not like that. The scholars are in agreement that the meaning of His saying, ﴿Only those who hear will respond, and the dead, Allah will raise them﴾ [al-An'am: 36], is that the meaning is: and the disbelievers, Allah will raise them.

We have already presented this, clarified by Qur'anic verses, in Surah "al-Naml," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ [al-Naml: 80], and the verse that follows.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, and you cannot make hear those who are in the graves﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this, and what has come concerning the hearing of the dead, in Surah "al-Naml," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾ and the verse that follows [al-Naml: 80].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 27:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colours? And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of varying colours, and jet-black ones.﴾ ﴿And among people and moving creatures and cattle are those of varying colours likewise.﴾ We have already discussed this in surah "al-Rum", in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and your colours﴾ [al-Rum: 22]. There we explained the indication of the verses that He, exalted and majestic, alone is the one who has effect, and that natures have no effect except by His will, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 32:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾. We have already discussed this verse, together with its counterparts among the verses of hope, by way of digression, and we mentioned the meaning of the wrongdoer (al-zalim), the moderate (al-muqtasid) and the foremost (al-sabiq), and the reason the wrongdoer is mentioned before them both in connection with the promise of the Gardens, in surah al-Nur, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin﴾, and the verse that follows [al-Nur: 22].

As for His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾, we have already dealt with it, along with the similar verses that resemble it, in surah al-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and that you may extract from it ornaments which you wear﴾.

The Qur'anic verse: ﴿And they will cry out therein, "Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do."﴾

I have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-A'raf," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth. So are there any intercessors for us to intercede for us, or could we be returned so we might do other than what we used to do?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 53] and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered your associates whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth﴾ — the verse. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Furqan," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they have taken gods besides Him who create nothing while they are themselves created﴾ [al-Furqan: 3]. And in Surah "al-Ra'd," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or have they set up for Allah associates who have created like His creation, so that the creation seemed alike to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ — the verse [al-Ra'd: 16].

Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they should cease [from their positions]﴾ ... the verse. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth, except by His permission﴾ [al-Hajj: 65].

The Words of Allah Most High: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that if a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾ — to the end of the verse. We have already discussed this in Surah "al-An'am" (Surah 6), in the discussion of His words: ﴿Or you should say, "If the Scripture had been revealed to us, we would surely have been better guided than they"﴾ [al-An'am: 157].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 43:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the evil plotting﴾.

This indicates that the plotting here is something other than the evil, and it was added to the evil because of the necessity of difference between the annexed noun (al-mudaf) and the noun it is annexed to (al-mudaf ilayh).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the evil plotting does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43], indicates that what is meant by al-mункар (the evil) here is the evil itself and nothing else, so the contradiction between the annexation construction (al-tarkib al-idafi) and the qualifying construction (al-tarkib al-taqyidi) is evident.

What appears, and God knows best, is that the correct view (al-tahqiq) is the permissibility of attributing a thing to itself when the wordings differ, because the difference between the wordings may suffice for the difference between the annexed noun and the noun it is annexed to, as Ibn Jarir firmly held in his tafsir in other than this place.

Ibn Malik alludes to this in his Khulasa (al-Khulasa, the versified grammar) with his saying:(p-376)

"If the two are singular nouns, annex decisively; otherwise follow the one that comes after."

As for his saying:

"A noun is not annexed to what is one with it in meaning, and interpret it when it occurs in a misleading way."

What appears after investigation is that there is no need to interpret it, despite its frequency in the Qur'an and in the Arabic language. The apparent view is that it is a stylistic feature of the Arabic idiom, as evidenced by how often it occurs, such as his saying here ﴿and the evil plotting﴾, and the plotting is the evil, as evidenced by his saying: ﴿And the evil plotting does not encompass [anyone]﴾, etc.; and such as his saying: ﴿And the Abode of the Hereafter﴾ [al-A'raf: 169], and the abode is the Hereafter; and such as his saying: ﴿The month of Ramadan﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], and the month is Ramadan in reality; and such as his saying: ﴿from the jugular vein﴾ [Qaf: 16], and the jugular (al-habl) is the vein (al-warid).

Its counterpart in Arabic speech is the saying of 'Antarah in his Mu'allaqa:

"And a full coat of mail whose gaps I tore open with the sword, against the protector of the essence, the marked one."

The original meaning of mishakk (with a kasra) is the strap with which the coat of mail is tightened, but 'Antarah here intended by it the coat of mail itself and annexed it to it, as is clear from his speech, because the act of tearing the gaps falls upon the coat of mail, not upon the strap with which it is tightened, as some verifiers firmly held, and this is evident, contrary to the apparent meaning of the words of the author of Taj al-'Arus, for he cited 'Antarah's verse as evidence that al-mishakk is the strap with which the coat of mail is tightened. Rather, the mishakk in this verse of 'Antarah is, in reality, the sabighah (the full coat of mail), and it was annexed to it as we have mentioned.

And the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"Like a virgin of the cultivated (muqanah), white with yellowness, nourished by the flowing water, unmixed."

Here al-bikr is in reality al-muqanah. As for what Ibn Malik held, the response is to interpret the annexed noun as meaning that what is meant by it is the named referent of the noun it is annexed to.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 35, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for what they have earned, He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature⦆ — the verse. We have already presented the verses that clarify it and its Arabic evidences in Surah "al-Nahl," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it a single creature⦆ — the verse [al-Nahl: 61].
